name: fetch

attributes.attribute: a Scottish and Irish folk figure
a kind of double of a person
a morning sighting promised long life
a night sighting limited life to the span of a hearth turf sod

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The fetch, also spelled feac, is a figure of Scottish and Irish folklore. MacKillop derives the name from Old Irish feccan and calls the being a fairy doppelganger. The belief held that each person had a companion double, called the fetch. Seeing this apparition in the early morning promised the viewer a long life. Seeing it at night was fatal. The viewer would live no longer than a sod of turf kept in the fireplace. Michael Traynor noted in The English Dialect of Donegal that the word had no Irish equivalent in Irish contexts.

okr.objective: The fetch entry explains the Scottish and Irish double figure and the omens tied to seeing it.
